title: Anyone get addicted to their own game?
author: diox__
selftext:
I have been working on iOS apps for about a year and a half now, and my latest iteration for one of them revived the spark that made me love it.

It feels weird to get addicted to your own supply, anyone else fall on the same boat?

My goal at making these games is to make it as pain free for the player, minimal optional ads (google ads only fuck applovin).. permanent monthly pass not a subscription… things like that I take a personal stance on, like I HATE that SO much. 

I know monetization says to go the other way, extract as much value as possible… but yah. 

So I guess also, does any one else also take a similar stance in their game dev?

comments.author: Galitzianer0
comments.body: Yes, I made a game like Ultima:  Exodus except with 14 different classes to choose from and fell in love with the game, I played it so damn much.  And other than some friends, I'm pretty much the only one lol.  Still, worth it, what a fun time it is

comments.author: Shleepy1
comments.body: Not addicted, but I enjoy playtesting a lot. Friends love it as well, amazing experience to iterate this fast.

comments.author: Russ_72days
comments.body: Ha yes! I revisited it after a few months to add some new animations (thanks to Claude and his mates) and it’s like a whole new game (for me anyway). I think in the not too distant future 50% of gamers will just be describing their own games and having them built on the fly. Kinda makes sense. You know what you like and what you’d like to see in a game.
